title: Landing Gear — Carbon Brake Remaining Stack Life Verification
abstract: Mandatory one-time verification of remaining carbon stack life by direct measurement, to find the brakes that the delivered wear pin has been over-reading on high-cycle aircraft.

sections.planning_reason: The wear pin as delivered reads against the pressure plate, which itself moves as the torque tube attachment relaxes. On a high-cycle aircraft the two effects cancel and the pin reads about eight per cent of stack life more than is really there. Two operators found brakes at zero remaining life during a wheel change that the pin had passed at the previous turnaround. The airworthiness authority has issued a directive requiring a one-time verification by direct measurement on the exposed population.
sections.description: This is an inspection Service Bulletin. Each brake on the affected aircraft is measured directly with a depth gauge from the torque tube flange rather than from the pressure plate, and the result is compared against the true wear limit given in the accomplishment instructions. Brakes found below the limit are removed. No modification is embodied.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Chock the aircraft and release the parking brake in accordance with the maintenance manual. WARNING: DO NOT APPROACH A BRAKE THAT HAS BEEN USED IN THE LAST HOUR. FUSIBLE PLUGS MAY RELEASE WITHOUT WARNING. Do AMM-S-32-40-11-200-050-A to gain access to the wear indicator at each brake. Measure the stack thickness with the depth gauge from the torque tube flange datum at three positions spaced one hundred and twenty degrees apart and record all three readings. Compare the smallest reading against the true wear limit table. Where the smallest reading is above the limit, no action is required and the brake may remain in service to its next scheduled check. Where the smallest reading is at or below the limit, remove the brake before further flight and fit a serviceable unit. Report every measurement to Aeralis using the form attached to this Service Bulletin, whether or not a brake is removed, so that the fleet wear model can be corrected.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30, SOLANO-34 and VANTOR-64 aircraft from MSN S00003 to MSN S01068 that carry the delivered wear pin datum. Aircraft from MSN S01068 onward carry the relocated datum in production and are not affected. Compliance is mandatory under the referenced airworthiness directive.
sections.material_note: No kit is required. Operators should hold at least one serviceable brake per station covered, since a finding at or below the limit cannot be deferred and the aircraft is grounded until the brake is changed.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 500 flight cycles or 3 months after the effective date of the referenced airworthiness directive, whichever occurs first.
